newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says OK Tedi copper barges halted.
newsitem.headline: BHP says OK Tedi copper barges halted.

text.p: Shipments of concentrates down the Fly River by barge from the Ok Tedi copper mine in Papua New Guinea have been halted by low water levels, the mine's operator, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, said on Tuesday.
Deliveries were being met from stockpiles, BHP said.
"As of yesterday (Monday), there was no barge movement," a BHP spokesman said from BHP's headquarters in Melbourne.
One barge carrying concentrates is being delayed at port of Kiunga, while several others have been stopped downriver.

Concentrates are transported by pipeline from the mine to the port of Kiunga, and then by barge down the Fly River for loading onto a silo vessel in the Gulf of Papua before being transferred to bulk carriers.
The spokesman could not say how much concentrate was on hand at the silo vessel.
"But typically, there are sufficent stockpiles on hand to deal with the seasonal dry period," the spokesman said. "There are no indications that deliveries are not being met," he said.
Ok Tedi produces about 600,000 tonnes of copper concentrate annually. The material is mainly shipped to Asia and Europe.
BHP owns 52.6 percent of the mine. The other partners are Canada's Inmet Mining Corp, with 17.4 percent and the Papua New Guinea government 30 percent.
